GREAT FORGE WITH THE HEART-CRYSTAL: a vaulted stone hall cut deep into the mountain's eastern shoulder, one huge arched furnace mouth breathing orange at its far end, a broad anvil on a stone dais set well off to one side, timber-and-iron gantries crossing overhead at three uneven heights, a great glowing heart-crystal set in the furnace's throat with chunky stepped sides burning amber from within

GREAT FORGE WITH THE FLOATING BLADE: a wide vaulted hall carved into the mountain's core, one great arched furnace mouth at the far wall, a broad anvil on a raised stone dais angled toward one corner, heavy timber gantries sagging at different pitches overhead, a finished blade hanging by itself in the air above the anvil drinking the warm orange light

GREAT FORGE WITH THE STONE FACE DOOR: a broad hall of rough-cut stone deep beneath the mountain's crown, one enormous arched furnace whose carved stone face fills the back wall with its open jaw as the fire door, a wide anvil on a stepped dais set to one side, three timber gantries crossing at staggered heights with the shortest hooked well away from the others

GREAT FORGE WITH THE CRACKED BELL: a vaulted stone hall dug into the mountain's northern root, one huge arched furnace mouth glowing at the far end, a broad anvil on a stone dais pushed toward the left wall, heavy iron-banded timbers overhead at uneven angles, a cracked dark bell hung in a low arch above the furnace glowing a soft amber along every crack

GREAT FORGE WITH THE SHRINE NICHE: a tall vaulted hall cut into the mountain beneath a thick cap of stone, one great arched furnace mouth dominating the back wall, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off-centre to the right, heavy timber gantries spanning the hall at three different heights, a shrine niche carved into the left pillar holding a worn pictorial relief of a flame and three lit candles

LAVA-FED SMITHY WITH THE FLOATING HAMMER: a low stone smithy with one wide arched furnace mouth low in its back wall, built over a bright molten channel running across its floor, a black stone bridge over it sitting off-centre toward the far wall, three stone sluice gates of different sizes set along one edge with the smallest pulled well aside, a heavy hammer hanging by itself in the air above the broad anvil

LAVA-FED SMITHY WITH THE SERPENT SPOUT: a forge hall built astride a bright molten channel that cuts through its floor from one rough wall to the other, a low black stone bridge crossing it off to one side, three stone sluice gates of unequal width along the near edge with the narrowest set apart, a carved serpent spout arching from the furnace wall dripping molten light into a worn stone bowl on the dais beside the anvil

LAVA-FED SMITHY WITH THE WARM EGG: a broad stone smithy straddling a bright molten channel whose glow rises through gaps in the stone floor, a single low black stone bridge set well to one side, three sluice gates of different heights along the far edge, a pale warm egg nested deep in the coal bed of the furnace mouth breathing soft gold

LAVA-FED SMITHY WITH THE LANTERN CHAIN: a wide forge hall with one great arched furnace mouth set deep in its far wall, built over a bright molten channel crossing its floor from a rough arch on the left, a black stone bridge off-centre to the right, three stone sluice gates of uneven width along the channel's near bank with the narrowest set apart, a lantern of trapped fire swinging on a long chain above the anvil casting flat bands of orange

CALDERA LEDGE WORKSHOP WITH THE HEART-CRYSTAL: a wide stone workshop on a broad ledge inside the mountain's open crater, the glowing throat far below throwing warm light upward, a roof of timber and hide stretched over rough posts at uneven heights, one deep arched furnace set into the inner rock face, the broad anvil on a stone dais near the ledge's edge, a great heart-crystal set in the furnace's throat with chunky stepped sides burning from within

CALDERA LEDGE WORKSHOP WITH THE CARVED SERPENT SPOUT: a sprawling workshop on a wide stone ledge inside the volcano's open throat, the glowing caldera far below, a roof of timber and hide sloping at an uneven pitch, one wide arched furnace mouth cut into the inner cliff, a broad anvil on a low stone dais set off to one side, a carved serpent spout above the furnace dripping molten light into a shallow stone bowl

CALDERA LEDGE WORKSHOP WITH THE FLOATING BLADE: a stone workshop set on a wide uneven ledge inside the mountain's open crater, the far wall open to the caldera's warm glow rising from below, a roof of hide and heavy timber spanning part of the space at a crooked angle, one arched furnace mouth cut deep into the cliff behind, a broad anvil on a stepped dais pushed toward one corner, a finished blade hanging by itself in the air above it

TOWER FORGE WITH THE STONE ARM BELLOWS: a tall narrow forge stacked up a chimney of stone deep inside the mountain, the furnace mouth wide and arched at the very bottom, a stair winding up one wall past two landings at uneven heights, a broad anvil on a dais set off-centre at the furnace level, a carved stone arm set into the wall working a large bellows with slow deliberate strokes

TOWER FORGE WITH THE GLOWING FLAME RELIEF: a tall narrow stone chimney forge cut into the mountain's spine, the great arched furnace at its base breathing orange upward, a stair climbing one wall on stepped stone pegs at irregular spacing, the broad anvil on a low stone dais leaning slightly off-centre, its flat side carrying a worn pictorial relief of a carved flame that glows softly from within the iron

TOWER FORGE WITH THE FLOATING STEPS: a narrow forge tower rising inside a chimney of rough mountain stone, the arched furnace mouth at the bottom throwing light up all the walls, a broad anvil on a dais set to one side of the furnace, a stair of floating stone steps curving up one wall at uneven intervals climbing toward the chimney throat above

CAVE FORGE BY THE POOL WITH THE CRACKED BELL: a low rough cave forge beside a still hot pool cut into the mountain's base, stalactites of uneven length hanging from the irregular ceiling, a worn stone floor sloping gently toward the water, one wide arched furnace set into the back wall, a broad anvil on a stone dais pushed to one side, a cracked dark bell in a low arch above the furnace glowing softly along its crack

CAVE FORGE BY THE POOL WITH THE SHRINE NICHE: a low rough cave forge opening beside a still steaming pool deep in the mountain, stalactites of seven uneven lengths overhead, a worn stone floor stepping down toward the water's edge, one arched furnace mouth set into the far wall, a broad anvil on a dais off to one corner, a shrine niche carved into the rock beside the furnace holding a worn pictorial relief of a hammer and three lit candles

CAVE FORGE BY THE POOL WITH THE WARM EGG: a rough low cave forge beside a still hot pool inside the mountain's root, stalactites of uneven length crowding the ceiling at one end and thinning at the other, a worn stone floor with an uneven step down near the anvil dais, one wide arched furnace set into the cave's back wall, a pale warm egg nestled in the coal bed glowing gold

OBSIDIAN HALL WITH THE STONE FACE DOOR: a hall of black glassy volcanic stone whose chunky stepped sides throw the fire back in flat amber bands, a wide arched furnace low in the back wall with a carved stone face filling it so the open jaw is the fire door, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off-centre to the right, a stair cut into the rock climbing one corner in uneven steps

OBSIDIAN HALL WITH THE HEART-CRYSTAL: a broad hall of black glassy volcanic stone deep inside the mountain with chunky stepped walls that catch the furnace glow in flat orange bands, one wide arched furnace at the far end, a broad anvil on a stepped stone dais angled toward one wall, a great heart-crystal set in the furnace's throat with chunky stepped sides burning bright amber from within

OBSIDIAN HALL WITH THE FLOATING HAMMER: a tall hall of black glassy volcanic stone whose chunky stepped sides throw the fire back in flat warm bands, one huge arched furnace mouth set low in the back wall, a broad anvil on an uneven stone dais pushed toward one corner, a heavy hammer hanging by itself in the still air above the anvil

OPEN-SIDED FLANK FORGE WITH THE LANTERN CHAIN: a forge hall high on the volcano's shoulder open through three wide arches of unequal span to the open air, one great arched furnace set into the inner mountain wall breathing orange, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off-centre beneath the narrowest arch, a lantern of trapped fire swinging on a long chain above the dais casting flat bands of warm gold

OPEN-SIDED FLANK FORGE WITH THE CARVED SERPENT SPOUT: a wide forge hall on the mountain's high flank open through three arches of different widths to the sky beyond, one deep arched furnace set into the solid rock at the back, a broad anvil on a low stone dais pushed toward one side, a carved serpent spout above the furnace mouth dripping molten light in a thin bright thread into a stone bowl on the floor beside the dais

BELLOWS-HOUSE FORGE WITH THE GLOWING HAMMER RELIEF: one wide arched furnace mouth breathing orange at the end of a broad timber-and-stone bellows hall inside the mountain, the broad anvil on a stone dais beside it carrying a worn pictorial relief of a carved hammer that glows softly from deep within the iron, a great timber wheel turning in a race of dark water off to one side, three bellows of different sizes along the wall with the smallest hooked well away from the others

BELLOWS-HOUSE FORGE WITH THE WARM EGG: one wide arched furnace mouth set in the end wall of a low stone-and-timber bellows hall cut into the mountain, a pale warm egg resting in its coal bed glowing soft gold, a broad anvil on an off-centre stone dais before it, a great timber wheel turning in a race of dark water set well to one side, three bellows of unequal size hanging from iron pins with the largest mounted higher than the rest
